title: Judge could order Nebius to halt data center construction in Independence
source_used: KSHB 41 Kansas City (the pool's FOX4KC item is blocked; KSHB reports the same lawsuit)
key_facts: A motions hearing is set for 22 Oct 2026 at 9 a.m. on a lawsuit related to Nebius's data centre project in Independence, Missouri.

The Independence GUARD (Guardians United Against Reckless Development) Alliance filed the lawsuit to halt construction of the project; residents along Bly Road want construction stopped near their homes.
The lawsuit alleges the city violated zoning and sunshine laws and the city charter, and has failed to enforce city laws.
The hearing covers the residents' motion for a temporary restraining order and the defendants' motion to dismiss.
Named defendants are the city of Independence, Missouri, ADC Holdings LLC (the data centre developer) and Independence Power Partners LP.
The city council approved billions of dollars in incentives for Dutch tech company Nebius in March; Nebius broke ground on the first phase in April.
The project is a 2.1-million-square-foot hyperscale AI data factory on 400 acres at the south end of Bly Road.

Nebius, through subsidiary Missouri ADC Holdings, is party to the lawsuit; John Sutter, Nebius vice president of public affairs, said: 'We are reviewing the claims and cannot comment on the case specifics.'
quote_evidence: A hearing has been set for October 22 at 9 a.m. on their motion for a temporary restraining order and the defendants’ motion to dismiss.
“We are reviewing the claims and cannot comment on the case specifics,” Nebius Vice President of Public Affairs John Sutter said in a statement.
The lawsuit alleges the city violated zoning and sunshine laws, as well as the city charter, and has failed to enforce city laws.
why_it_matters_hint: A court fight over a large AI data centre in Independence; no ruling yet, and the claims are allegations.
event_date: Lawsuit filed earlier in 2026; hearing set in the report dated 8 Oct 2026
